title: Kotodama: a new grammar game from scratch
question: This is a playable prototype, not pictures: play it at https://fumbleforce.github.io/tower-of-words/game3d/minigames/kotodama.html (phone or desktop, about four minutes). It's a new game, started over after "even less fun, start over, write a new game from scratch, make it the most fun and impressive grammar game in existence". Is this fun? Round 2 (after your note: translations cut off, too casual, instructions unclear): the first twelve pictures show the fixes. Same game; the translations fit at every size, people speak politely (～さん, ください, です/ます; the machines still get plain だして), and the first command is a three-step walkthrough with a hand. Round 3 (after "kotodama: fun, keep going with it"; tapping over dragging, better machines): the first seven pictures. Same game. The vending machine, hot-water pot and fridge are redrawn with idle motion and a dispense, and the drinks are redrawn to match. Every action was already a tap; now a unit test keeps it that way, and the particle buttons pulse while a word waits for its particle.

options.label: kotodama: fun, keep going with it
options.note: The pitch: B2 after six, and the old machines do exactly what Eric says, word for word. You build each command from the room itself (tap who and what, give each a particle, then fire the verb), and the particles decide what flies where. Requests pile up faster than one command can answer them one at a time, so と (two or three people served in one sentence) is the combo you need, scored 2 × 2 or 3 × 3 with a streak on top. Between shifts you pick a power word: も, みんな, まって or ください. Three shifts, three hearts, a daily run with a best score. The design page, with what it borrows and an honest check, is game3d/minigames/README.md (Kotodama). The screens come from a headless run of the daily seed; the frame strips are from game3d/minigames/tools/frames.mjs.

options.label: not-fun: not it yet
options.note: Say what's missing in the comment and it goes into the next round.

decision: Kotodama picked: keep going (tap-only and better machines done in 246fd2df, 61ab7bce)
